@kevdude wants us all to promise we'll never change our current model. While it's working reasonably well so far, it's still far from a proven model. As such, I and some of the mods believe we need to maintain the flexibility to react to scenarios we haven't encountered yet - some of which may require moderator intervention. @kevdude suggested that moderators not willing to promise the current system will never change should step down, and called for us to have an official vote on this.

Under our constitution, we can't make mods "promise something or step down", so the simplest option is the above motion. If it passes, mods will be called upon to make the pledge that the current system won't change. If they choose not to make that pledge, then there is no consequence. If the motion fails, mods could still choose individually to make that pledge, again with no consequence if they don't do it. As such the motion doesn't achieve much, but it is what was requested and it was seconded, so we really have no choice but to vote on it.

If the motion did pass, we could strengthen it by voting to amend the constitution to make it mandatory, but that would require unanimous agreement from the mods. Given two mods have already voted against this motion, I think it is extremely unlikely that motion would get support.
